text:
janet_account: forwarding from customer (Faber Health) - they found a handful of presigned download links indexed by a public crawler. customer thinks links came from our private VPC. example: https://faber-downloads.redwood.private/signed?X=abc123
sara_support: acknowledged. pinging security. @mike_security can you take lead on triage? :eyes:
mike_security: on it. janet - which deployment type is this? private VPC or dedicated?
janet_account: Private VPC in eu-west-1. tenant id: faber-0842. they said links look like our file-service presigned URLs for attachments.
olga_engineer: ok. first ask: were these presigned URLs generated by the app (service account) or by a backend job? any recent RBAC/IAM changes to the service account that touches S3/objects?
mike_security: @olga_engineer good call. can you check recent IAM/RBAC changes for faber-0842 since 2026-11-01? specifically any policy that added s3:* or wildcard resources.
olga_engineer: pulling policy audit now. also starting a search for KMS Decrypt events tied to faber keys.
infra_bot: log-export job queued: export-audit-faber-0842 (started). request id = lg-4a9c. ETA ~90s.
olga_engineer: found one change: 2026-11-08 03:24 UTC - role "faber-app-svc" had a policy patch that added `s3:GetObject` on `arn:aws:s3:::faber-uploads/*` and a testing branch accidentally used `Resource: "*"`. rollout flag removed later but change window overlaps when customer says links were created.
mike_security: that matches the timeframe. need to confirm which service principal called presigned generation API. search for generate_presigned_url patterns in our gateway/api logs.
elyes_oncall: I'm on logs. querying object-service access and our API gateway logs for faber-0842 between 2026-11-08T02:50:00Z and 2026-11-08T04:00:00Z.
elyes_oncall: results: found 7 generate_presigned_url calls from IP 34.120.9.22 using service-account token svc-faber-app-xy. timestamps align.
olga_engineer: svc-faber-app-xy is the one with the temporary wildcard policy. looks like the service account itself performed the ops - likely a mis-scoped permission allowed an automated job to create broadly-scoped links, not an external exploit.
mike_security: containment - 1) rotate the service-account token 2) revoke the temporary RBAC patch 3) disable presigned generation for public buckets until confirmed. janet - please send this containment checklist to the customer; keep it short and actionable.
janet_account: drafting customer message: "We've paused presigned URL generation for your tenant, rotated the service token, and are pulling logs. We will follow up with a list of affected links and recommended rotation steps within 2 hours." sending.
sara_support: cc @faber-secoutreach (customer wants status updates every 30m).
mike_security: @olga_engineer - double-check KMS Decrypt logs for tenant master key and any CMKs used for object encryption. need to ensure no unauthorized Decrypts.
olga_engineer: querying KMS: Decrypt events where principal = svc-faber-app-xy or tenant = faber-0842 between window. also checking KeyPolicy changes.
infra_bot: s3-access-log-export ready: /exports/faber-0842/s3-20261108.gz
elyes_oncall: found 0 KMS Decrypt API calls from unknown principals. decrypts were from svc-faber-app-xy and normal app workers with expected IP ranges. no access from outside infra.
mike_security: suggests misconfig created links but no external KMS decrypt. next, enumerate created links and TTLs; customer reported crawler hits so some links had long TTLs.
olga_engineer: running DB query: 
```
SELECT id, key, expires_at, created_by, ttl_seconds FROM presigned_links WHERE tenant = 'faber-0842' AND created_at BETWEEN '2026-11-08 02:50' AND '2026-11-08 04:00';
```
results: 24 links created; 6 with ttl > 7 days. created_by = svc-faber-app-xy job-run-id=run-7b2.
mike_security: mark those 6 as high priority revoke. generate revoke set and push invalidate job.
elyes_oncall: invalidation job submitted: `rwdctl presigned invalidate --tenant faber-0842 --ids id1,id2,id3,id4,id5,id6`
infra_bot: invalidation complete. 6 links revoked.
janet_account: forwarding revoke confirmation to customer. asking customer for any external IPs they saw accessing links before revocation.
elyes_oncall: checking S3 GETs on those keys prior to invalidation: found 3 unique external IPs: 198.51.100.12, 203.0.113.5, 172.68.34.101 - each performed a single GET within the window.
mike_security: log those accesses and open threat-hunting ticket. check if IPs belong to known crawlers/bots and enrich IOCs.
sara_support: created SOC ticket #SOC-2026-114 for enrichment and IOCs, assigning @mike_security.
mike_security: remediation/post-incident actions: - patch RBAC rollout pipeline to disallow wildcard resources in testing branches - add pre-deploy lint failing on Resource:"*" for production service roles - add alert: presigned URL creation spike per tenant (threshold: >10 in 10min)
olga_engineer: will open infra PR for lint and canary test. propose reducing default presigned TTL to 24h unless explicitly approved.
janet_account: customer requested a formal report with timeline. mike - can you produce a brief timeline and impact summary by EOD? include affected link count, external accesses, containment actions.
mike_security: will draft and send to janet for delivery. recommending mandatory rotation for any long-lived signing keys; we can provide rotation scripts.
elyes_oncall: final check: no remaining active long-lived links, service token rotated, RBAC rolled back. monitoring enabled for 48h.
janet_account: customer replied: "Thanks - appreciate the quick response. We'll wait for the full report." :thumbsup:
mike_security: closing thread after report is sent. scheduling postmortem with eng-runtime & infra to add rollout guardrails. owners: olga (infra lint), sara (alerts), janet (customer comms), elyes (monitoring), mike (postmortem + report).
sara_support: adding runbook change: notify account before RBAC patches that widen resource scope.
mike_security: noted. moving to draft postmortem.
